grounding.excerpt: *4 Once per permit term. The test is to be performed during the first springtime after the permit effective date, during the irrigation season
shall become effective on January 1, 2022. This permit and the authorization to discharge shall expire at midnight, December 31, 2026.
No evidence in this packet that the once-per-term WET test was or was not performed.

rationale: The packet states the once-per-term WET test must occur during the first springtime after the January 1, 2022 effective date and defines the FY2025 window, but it does not establish whether that once-per-term obligation was satisfied or remains outstanding. Per the oracle relation contract, special_monitoring_window_applies is UNRESOLVED when outstanding performance status cannot be established. Although the scheduling clause points to a first-spring window (spring 2022, not FY2025), that timing alone does not ground ACCEPT (FY2025 is not established as a required WET year) or REJECT (FY2025 is not established as not required) without resolving whether the term obligation is still open. Preferring unsupported uncertainty to unsupported semantic closure, UNRESOLVED is the correct disposition.
